    function setGoogleOneTapZindex() {
        const spMessageContainer = document.querySelector('div[id^="sp_message_container_"]');
        const googleOneTap = document.querySelector('[id^="credential_picker_"]');

        console.log("GSZ: spMessageContainer", spMessageContainer)
        console.log("GSZ: googleOneTap", googleOneTap)

        if (googleOneTap && spMessageContainer) {
            const originalZIndex = window.getComputedStyle(spMessageContainer).zIndex;
            const numericZIndex = parseInt(originalZIndex, 10);

            if (!isNaN(numericZIndex)) {
                spMessageContainer.style.zIndex = (numericZIndex - 1).toString();
                googleOneTap.style.zIndex = numericZIndex.toString();
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Sync Sourcepoint consent status to backend
     * @param {string|undefined} consentUUID - Consent UUID from Sourcepoint (undefined for non-GDPR)
     * @param {object} info - Consent info object from Sourcepoint
     */
    function sendConsentToBackend(consentUUID, info) {
        const payload = {
            consentUUID: consentUUID ?? null,
            consentedToAll: info.consentedToAll ?? null,
            applies: info.applies ?? null,
            categories: info.categories ?? {}
        };

        console.log('Syncing consent payload:', payload);

        // Wait for DOM to be ready to ensure page request has completed
        const sendConsent = () => {
            fetch('/consent', {
                method: 'POST',
                headers: {
                    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
                    'Accept': 'application/json',
                    'X-CSRF-TOKEN': '3CDyBDmJxSaiWRADRLxXp0RhklnsPPxcqZ9T3ZyH',
                },
                body: JSON.stringify(payload)
            })
                .then(response => {
                    if (!response.ok) {
                        throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
                    }
                    return response.json();
                })
                .then(data => console.log('Consent synced:', data))
                .catch(err => console.error('Consent sync failed:', err));
        };

        // If DOM already loaded, send immediately. Otherwise wait.
        if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', sendConsent);
        } else {
            sendConsent();
        }
    }

    
    function spTrafficTargeting(search) {
        const params = new URLSearchParams(search);
        const utmValue = (name) => {
            const value = (params.get(name) ?? '').trim().toLowerCase();

            if (value === '') {
                return 'none';
            }

            return /^[a-z0-9_.-]+$/.test(value) ? value.slice(0, 50) : 'other';
        };

        return {
            utm_source: utmValue('utm_source'),
            utm_medium: utmValue('utm_medium'),
        };
    }

    window.mnSpInitialConsent;
    window._sp_queue = [];
    window._sp_ = {
        config: {
            accountId: 1896,

            baseEndpoint: "https://sp.mumsnet.com",
            gdpr: {
                targetingParams: {
                    premium:  false ,
                    ...spTrafficTargeting(window.location.search),
                },
            },
            events: {
                onMessageReady: function (message_type) {
                    console.log('onMessageReady ', message_type)

                    setGoogleOneTapZindex();
                },
                onMessageChoiceSelect: function (message_type, choice_id, choice_type_id) {
                    console.log('onMessageChoiceSelect message_type: ', message_type);

                    console.log('onMessageChoiceSelect choice_type_id: ', choice_type_id);
                },
                onPrivacyManagerAction: function (message_type, pmData) {
                    console.log('onPrivacyManagerAction message_type:', message_type);
                    console.log('onPrivacyManagerAction', pmData)
                },
                onConsentReady: function (message_type, consentUUID, euconsent, info) {
                    console.log("SOURCEPOINT CMP: consent ready");

                    performance.mark("cmp-script-loaded");
                    performance.measure("cmp_wrapper_latency", { start: 0, end: "cmp-script-loaded" });

                    sendConsentToBackend(consentUUID, info);

                    
                    console.log('AMPLITUDE: mnSpInitialConsent = ', info.consentedToAll)

                    const eventPayload = {
                        detail: {

                        }
                    };
                    
                    console.log('AMPLITUDE: dispatching event mn-sp-cmp-consent-set', eventPayload)
                    window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("mn-sp-cmp-consent-set", eventPayload));
                },
            },
        },
    };

    (function () {
        try {
            const state = window.globalState;
            if (!state?.user?.is_logged_in) return;

            const localTheme = window.localStorage?.getItem("theme");
            const cookieTheme = document.cookie
                .split("; ")
                .find((row) => row.startsWith("theme="))
                ?.split("=")[1];
            const rawPreference = localTheme || cookieTheme || "light";
            const preference = ["light", "dark", "system"].includes(
                rawPreference
            )
                ? rawPreference
                : "light";
            const prefersDark =
                window.matchMedia &&
                window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches;
            const active =
                preference === "dark" ||
                (preference === "system" && prefersDark)
                    ? "dark"
                    : "light";

            const root = document.documentElement;
            root.setAttribute("data-theme", preference);
            root.classList.remove("light", "dark", "system");
            root.classList.add(active);
        } catch (error) {
            // Fail closed: leave the default theme to avoid breaking page load.
        }
    })();
</script>

    function setGoogleOneTapZindex() {
        const spMessageContainer = document.querySelector('div[id^="sp_message_container_"]');
        const googleOneTap = document.querySelector('[id^="credential_picker_"]');

        console.log("GSZ: spMessageContainer", spMessageContainer)

    /**
     * Sync Sourcepoint consent status to backend
     * @param {string|undefined} consentUUID - Consent UUID from Sourcepoint (undefined for non-GDPR)
     * @param {object} info - Consent info object from Sourcepoint
     */
    function sendConsentToBackend(consentUUID, info) {
        const payload = {
            consentUUID: consentUUID ?? null,
            consentedToAll: info.consentedToAll ?? null,
            applies: info.applies ?? null,
            categories: info.categories ?? {}
        };

        console.log('Syncing consent payload:', payload);

        // Wait for DOM to be ready to ensure page request has completed
        const sendConsent = () => {
            fetch('/consent', {
                method: 'POST',
                headers: {
                    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
                    'Accept': 'application/json',
                    'X-CSRF-TOKEN': '07maa9ExRTbouRlZ2Ye3dYAPRDYucB8gSP2i5WkN',
                },
                body: JSON.stringify(payload)
            })
                .then(response => {
                    if (!response.ok) {
                        throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
                    }
                    return response.json();
                })
                .then(data => console.log('Consent synced:', data))
                .catch(err => console.error('Consent sync failed:', err));
        };

        // If DOM already loaded, send immediately. Otherwise wait.
        if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', sendConsent);
        } else {
            sendConsent();
        }
    }

    
    function spTrafficTargeting(search) {
        const params = new URLSearchParams(search);
        const utmValue = (name) => {
            const value = (params.get(name) ?? '').trim().toLowerCase();

            if (value === '') {
                return 'none';
            }

            return /^[a-z0-9_.-]+$/.test(value) ? value.slice(0, 50) : 'other';
        };

        return {
            utm_source: utmValue('utm_source'),
            utm_medium: utmValue('utm_medium'),
        };
    }

    (function () {
        try {
            const state = window.globalState;
            if (!state?.user?.is_logged_in) return;

            const localTheme = window.localStorage?.getItem("theme");
            const cookieTheme = document.cookie
                .split("; ")
                .find((row) => row.startsWith("theme="))
                ?.split("=")[1];
            const rawPreference = localTheme || cookieTheme || "light";
            const preference = ["light", "dark", "system"].includes(
                rawPreference
            )
                ? rawPreference
                : "light";
            const prefersDark =
                window.matchMedia &&
                window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches;
            const active =
                preference === "dark" ||
                (preference === "system" && prefersDark)
                    ? "dark"
                    : "light";

            const root = document.documentElement;
            root.setAttribute("data-theme", preference);
            root.classList.remove("light", "dark", "system");
            root.classList.add(active);
        } catch (error) {
            // Fail closed: leave the default theme to avoid breaking page load.
        }
    })();

    function setGoogleOneTapZindex() {
        const spMessageContainer = document.querySelector('div[id^="sp_message_container_"]');
        const googleOneTap = document.querySelector('[id^="credential_picker_"]');

        console.log("GSZ: spMessageContainer", spMessageContainer)
        console.log("GSZ: googleOneTap", googleOneTap)

        if (googleOneTap && spMessageContainer) {
            const originalZIndex = window.getComputedStyle(spMessageContainer).zIndex;
            const numericZIndex = parseInt(originalZIndex, 10);

            if (!isNaN(numericZIndex)) {
                spMessageContainer.style.zIndex = (numericZIndex - 1).toString();
                googleOneTap.style.zIndex = numericZIndex.toString();
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Sync Sourcepoint consent status to backend
     * @param {string|undefined} consentUUID - Consent UUID from Sourcepoint (undefined for non-GDPR)
     * @param {object} info - Consent info object from Sourcepoint
     */
    function sendConsentToBackend(consentUUID, info) {
        const payload = {
            consentUUID: consentUUID ?? null,
            consentedToAll: info.consentedToAll ?? null,
            applies: info.applies ?? null,
            categories: info.categories ?? {}
        };

        console.log('Syncing consent payload:', payload);

        // Wait for DOM to be ready to ensure page request has completed
        const sendConsent = () => {
            fetch('/consent', {
                method: 'POST',
                headers: {
                    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
                    'Accept': 'application/json',
                    'X-CSRF-TOKEN': 'Yht6ITLGLEbThMV8PuIeQ2iREdQNhebxygQ2U8vk',
                },
                body: JSON.stringify(payload)
            })
                .then(response => {
                    if (!response.ok) {
                        throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
                    }
                    return response.json();
                })
                .then(data => console.log('Consent synced:', data))
                .catch(err => console.error('Consent sync failed:', err));
        };

        // If DOM already loaded, send immediately. Otherwise wait.
        if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', sendConsent);
        } else {
            sendConsent();
        }
    }

    
    function spTrafficTargeting(search) {
        const params = new URLSearchParams(search);
        const utmValue = (name) => {
            const value = (params.get(name) ?? '').trim().toLowerCase();

            if (value === '') {
                return 'none';
            }

            return /^[a-z0-9_.-]+$/.test(value) ? value.slice(0, 50) : 'other';
        };

        return {
            utm_source: utmValue('utm_source'),
            utm_medium: utmValue('utm_medium'),
        };
    }

            events: {

                },

                    console.log('onPrivacyManagerAction message_type:', message_type);
                    console.log('onPrivacyManagerAction', pmData)
                },
                onConsentReady: function (message_type, consentUUID, euconsent, info) {
                    console.log("SOURCEPOINT CMP: consent ready");

                    performance.mark("cmp-script-loaded");
                    performance.measure("cmp_wrapper_latency", { start: 0, end: "cmp-script-loaded" });

                    sendConsentToBackend(consentUUID, info);

                    
                    console.log('AMPLITUDE: mnSpInitialConsent = ', info.consentedToAll)
                    window.mnSpInitialConsent = info.consentedToAll;
                    window.mnSpConsentReadyInfo = info

                    const eventPayload = {
                        detail: {

                            consentedToAll: info.consentedToAll
                        }
                    };
                    
                    console.log('AMPLITUDE: dispatching event mn-sp-cmp-consent-set', eventPayload)
                    window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("mn-sp-cmp-consent-set", eventPayload));
                },
            },
        },
    };

    (function () {
        try {
            const state = window.globalState;
            if (!state?.user?.is_logged_in) return;

            const localTheme = window.localStorage?.getItem("theme");
            const cookieTheme = document.cookie
                .split("; ")
                .find((row) => row.startsWith("theme="))
                ?.split("=")[1];
            const rawPreference = localTheme || cookieTheme || "light";
            const preference = ["light", "dark", "system"].includes(
                rawPreference
            )
                ? rawPreference
                : "light";
            const prefersDark =
                window.matchMedia &&
                window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches;
            const active =
                preference === "dark" ||
                (preference === "system" && prefersDark)
                    ? "dark"
                    : "light";

            const root = document.documentElement;
            root.setAttribute("data-theme", preference);
            root.classList.remove("light", "dark", "system");
            root.classList.add(active);
        } catch (error) {
            // Fail closed: leave the default theme to avoid breaking page load.
        }
    })();

                    <script>
        (() => {
            const flag = "mn_pagecache_probe";
            const enabled = (() => {
                try {
                    return localStorage.getItem(flag) === "on";
                } catch (_) {
                    return false;
                }
            })();

            if (!enabled || window.__MN_PAGECACHE_PROBE_INSTALLED__) return;
            window.__MN_PAGECACHE_PROBE_INSTALLED__ = true;

            const marker = "__MN_PAGECACHE_PROBE__";
            const version = "1.0.2";

            const navEntry = () => performance.getEntriesByType?.("navigation")?.[0];

            const payload = (eventName, event) => ({
                marker,
                version,
                capturedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
                event: eventName,
                persisted:
                    typeof event?.persisted === "boolean" ? event.persisted : null,
                url: location.href,
                visibilityState: document.visibilityState,
                hasFocus: document.hasFocus(),
                navigationType: navEntry()?.type || null,
                historyLength: history.length,
                performanceNow: Math.round(performance.now()),
                resources: performance.getEntriesByType?.("resource")?.length ?? null,
                dom: {
                    elements: document.getElementsByTagName("*").length,
                    iframes: document.querySelectorAll("iframe").length,
                    scripts: document.scripts.length,
                    images: document.images.length,
                },
            });

            const record = (eventName, event) => {
                console.log(marker, JSON.stringify(payload(eventName, event)));
            };

            addEventListener("pageshow", (event) => record("pageshow", event), true);
            addEventListener("pagehide", (event) => record("pagehide", event), true);
            addEventListener(
                "visibilitychange",
                (event) => {
                    record("visibilitychange", event);
                },
                true
            );

            record("probe-installed");
        })();
    </script>

We used to give each other a Christmas present, now I buy one for her and she buys three for our family.</p>\n<p>Here’s the thing (and I’m sure I’ll sound a bit ungrateful). Her presents are always, always “wrong”. She thinks about what we’d like but never asks and I do see her thought process but for at least 10 years there’s not one present that any of us have liked/wanted/needed. We all thank her, the children write thank you cards and things go straight to the charity shop (or the bin).</p>\n<p>Duff gifts (that show thought from her) have included:<br>\n• random viral toy she’s seen online that is great fun for 5 mins and then never touched again.<br>\n• one of my children has coeliac so she has several times sent gf baked goods, but they have also been vegan and were so, so awful (love food that is naturally vegan, none of us are keen on highly processed stuff - even the children didn’t like the last batch of gf/vegan doughnuts)<br>\n• large, random vases/jugs/mugs that are nothing like anything else we have and are “statement” pieces.<br>\n• clothes age 6-7 for a child who is 7 years and 10 months (this has happened a few times over the years). When I’ve said “the tshirt is lovely but might be a bit small, could I exchange it?” it’s always from a niche independent shop in Edinburgh or a Christmas market she went to last year in Bath and “saved for this year so it would be the right size”.</p>\n<p>I feel so ungrateful. I just dread her presents. There is always significant expense involved too - I’d estimate she spends at least £150 on us as a family, often more.</p>\n<p>For the last few years I have chatted to her very early on (October) and said “I’m trying to be super organised this year and I’d love some ideas of things you might like” in the hope that she will ask me too. But she doesn’t!! She says “ooh, I’ll have a think!” And then comes back with a short list.</p>\n<p>This year, I bit the bullet and said “all Kate is interested in this year is X so anything related to that or a voucher would be popular and I know Dan would like the Beano annual” (not real names 😂). She didn’t reply.</p>\n<p>I am a solo parent and while we’re not hard up, the WASTE of her money each year makes me feel so frustrated. And the pretence to be so grateful - I am grateful yo be thought of but not for the really duff presents.</p>\n<p>Any ideas? Suggesting no presents won’t work. I’m married with 3 children, whereas they’re childless and boyfriendless. I’ve moved to London, they’re still living in the little village we grew up and have never moved out. Obviously, there’s nothing wrong with that, and I’m not suggesting they should have the same lives as me. But I increasingly feel we have absolutely nothing in common. Our conversations are always very surface-level. Things like how’s your mum, congratulations on your sister getting engaged, Berlin is a lovely place how was your holiday, your children are cute, what a lovely brunch etc. Their mum still cooks their breakfast, any annual leave is spent travelling with parents or, rarely, a girls’ trip. There’s nothing particularly wrong with any of it, but I don’t feel like we’re having meaningful conversations or that I particularly look forward to seeing them.</p>\n<p>They’ll suggest arranging a Christmas get-together, basically saying they’re free any weekend in December and I’ll find myself looking at the dates and getting a sinking feeling that I can’t say I’m busy literally every weekend and every evening (although I’ve previously done that for a summer catch up). Or I’ll actually go and spend a rare child-free evening sitting there thinking what a waste of a night this is. They’re happy to come to where I live but because it’s a 1hr journey they obviously can’t come for a 5 min coffee.</p>\n<p>I also find that I have very little interest in hearing about their careers or their (non existent) dating lives. I know that sounds awful, but I just don’t feel invested in those things anymore. I think part of what makes this difficult is the history. We’ve grown up together, shared so many milestones and they’ve stood beside me at my wedding. It feels almost wrong to consider walking away from friendships that have been such a big part of my life. I think I’m holding onto them purely because of how long we’ve known each other, rather than because I actually enjoy the friendships now.</p>\n<p>Am I being unnecessarily dismissive and should I make more effort to maintain these friendships? Or is it perfectly reasonable to accept that we’ve grown apart?</p>\n<p>And, practically speaking, how do you drop a friendship like this without causing a huge drama? Do you just stop responding, politely decline invitations and let things naturally fizzle out? Or do you actually have a conversation? I don’t want a big falling-out or to hurt anyone. I just don’t really want to keep making time for friendships that I’m no longer enjoying.</p>\n","created_at":"2026-11-15T21:15:58+00:00","updated_at":"2026-11-16T03:23:35+00:00","link":"https://www.mumsnet.com/talk/am_i_being_unreasonable/5600133-to-let-my-friendship-with-childhood-besties-fizzle-out","replies_count":107,"sponsor":null,"is_excluded_from_search_engines":false,"topic":{"id":2724,"name":"AIBU?","slug":"am_i_being_unreasonable","link":"https://www.mumsnet.com/talk/am_i_being_unreasonable","category_id":9,"is_category_favourite":true,"is_excluded_from_search_engines":false,"is_geolocatable":false,"is_pollable":true,"default_poll_template_id":1,"add_poll_by_default":true,"is_payable":false,"fee":null,"is_premium":false,"can_view_threads":true,"can_create_thread":false,"is_followed_topic":false,"is_user_topic":false,"popular_topic":null,"new_users_can_not_post_for_x_days":null,"prevent_user_replies":false},"non_safe_images_exists":false,"poll":{"id":186321,"title":"Am mt-2 flex flex-col gap-2" id="item-5599992__content"><!--[--><!----><div class="prose break-words leading-6 text-card-foreground line-clamp-2"><p>We are spending the festive period at SIL and BIL. They will have a full house with us, my PIL, between us 5 kids, and 2 dogs - not to mention 4 more adults from SIL side who are local and joining us on Christmas Day. Safe to say it will be hectic fun!!!</p>
<p>I have been asked to contribute to dinner, in principle I have no problem with this, it must be daunting, expensive, and exhausting to host so many people for multiple days, and I am a good cook. However, I have been asked to make a tiramisu for those of us who don’t like Christmas pudding to have as dessert on 25th. This leaves me with 3 options, none of which I like -</p>
<ol><li>Make the tiramisu and bring it with me. Since we are travelling on 21st I would have to make this on 20th and with it being so rich with dairy I worry about it lasting, and not sure the texture would be as pleasant after so many days? I have no idea how a massive tiramisu will fit in the fridge with all the other food. Plus we have a 4 hour drive with all mine, DH, and kids stuff and I just don’t know if I will have space for a huge cool bag.</li><li>Make it there. I would have to go out to the shops and cook in an unfamiliar kitchen, all the while getting under SIL feet - an absolutely lovely woman, but quite highly strung. </li><li>Buy one from a supermarket there. A serious a downgrade on a proper homemade one. </li></ol>
<p>What I’m wondering is whether it would be acceptable for me to reply and ask if she would consider talking a monetary contribution instead. I was thinking £150 for my family unit - substantially more than ingredient cost.</p>

class="prose break-words leading-6 text-card-foreground line-clamp-2"><p>I’d love some advice…</p>
<p>I have a long standing friend (since school) who is single with no children. She really enjoys giving presents.</p>
<p>I have two children. We used to give each other a Christmas present, now I buy one for her and she buys three for our family.</p>
<p>Here’s the thing (and I’m sure I’ll sound a bit ungrateful). Her presents are always, always “wrong”. She thinks about what we’d like but never asks and I do see her thought process but for at least 10 years there’s not one present that any of us have liked/wanted/needed. We all thank her, the children write thank you cards and things go straight to the charity shop (or the bin).</p>
<p>Duff gifts (that show thought from her) have included:<br>
• random viral toy she’s seen online that is great fun for 5 mins and then never touched again.<br>
• one of my children has coeliac so she has several times sent gf baked goods, but they have also been vegan and were so, so awful (love food that is naturally vegan, none of us are keen on highly processed stuff - even the children didn’t like the last batch of gf/vegan doughnuts)<br>
• large, random vases/jugs/mugs that are nothing like anything else we have and are “statement” pieces.<br>
• clothes age 6-7 for a child who is 7 years and 10 months (this has happened a few times over the years). When I’ve said “the tshirt is lovely but might be a bit small, could I exchange it?” it’s always from a niche independent shop in Edinburgh or a Christmas market she went to last year in Bath and “saved for this year so it would be the right size”.</p>
<p>I feel so ungrateful. I just dread her presents. There is always significant expense involved too - I’d estimate she spends at least £150 on us as a family, often more.</p>
<p>For the last few years I have chatted to her very early on (October) and said “I’m trying to be super organised this year and I’d love some ideas of things you might like” in the hope that she will ask me too. But she doesn’t!! She says “ooh, I’ll have a think!” And then comes back with a short list.</p>
<p>This year, I bit the bullet and said “all Kate is interested in this year is X so anything related to that or a voucher would be popular and I know Dan would like the Beano annual” (not real names 😂). She didn’t reply.</p>
<p>I am a solo parent and while we’re not hard up, the WASTE of her money each year makes me feel so frustrated. And the pretence to be so grateful - I am grateful yo be thought of but not for the really duff presents.</p>
<p>Any ideas? Suggesting no presents won’t work. She will insist on carrying on even if I don’t buy her anything.</p>
<p>Also, I’m 99% confident that she likes my presents because I either get her things she’s suggested or I buy her practical/thoughtful things like a garden voucher and new gardening gloves (she’s a very keen gardener).</p>

leading-6 text-card-foreground line-clamp-2"><p>Because I genuinely need help navigating this and building my own.<br>
after a childhood in and out of care I have, by a combination of finding good mentors, a voracious reading habit (and ignoring the many, many times this was mocked in various placements) and being in top sets through sheer hard work rather than natural intelligence I have a well respected, aspirational job that I love.<br>
Thanks in no small part to MN I ‘mask’/fit in with the upper middle class around me in clothes, grooming and so forth. I’m not looking to imitate them if that makes sense but instead to navigate my way through what I missed as a child. I know nothing about classical music, opera or art. I am educating myself about philosophy at the moment after an interesting conversation I was part of (well, I didn’t have much to contribute tbh but you get the idea).<br>
I feel like I have a lot of gaps that I want to plug, not because I don’t feel as good as other people more that I want to get behind the curtain and see what’s there.<br>
if anyone has any suggestions about where to start as an adult - for example I have only found kids books describing the ballet for those who don’t know anything about it -  navigating any aspect of this, 🙏<br>
I’m happy to watch docs, read, listen. Don’t have limitless time and money but am happy to commit both realistically. The only thing I don’t need help with are our ‘classsics’ on the book world, EH, NT, skiing and horseriding (waaay to much open air).</p></div><!--[--><!----><!----><!--]--><!--]--></div><div <p>His family lives abroad and we are staying with them for Xmas (and planning for other seasonal holidays). He has painted himself as a victim, and am sure they think I've treated him terribly by ending the relationship.</p>
<p>What should I say to them at Xmas when they ask about the break up? I don't want to be petty, but also don't want them to think that I'm some monster and he's a poor victim, in case that becomes the narrative when DD grows up (she's 18m now). I haven't heard from his family since the break up 3 months ago, although we used to get on well.</p>
<p>AIBU: don't say much, just say we work better as coparents, and take the "high road".<br>
AINBU: tell them being with him was like having a second child, he is lazy and selfish, and I didn't want to set such a bad example of a romantic relationship to our DD? (Ie the truth)</p>
<p>Or something else?</p>

mt-2 flex flex-col gap-2" id="item-5600133__content"><!--[--><!----><div class="prose break-words leading-6 text-card-foreground line-clamp-2"><p>I’ve been friends with this group since we were children, they were my bridesmaids but I’m increasingly finding myself questioning why I’m still maintaining these friendships.</p>
<p>We’re now at very different stages of life. I’m married with 3 children, whereas they’re childless and boyfriendless. I’ve moved to London, they’re still living in the little village we grew up and have never moved out. Obviously, there’s nothing wrong with that, and I’m not suggesting they should have the same lives as me. But I increasingly feel we have absolutely nothing in common. Our conversations are always very surface-level. Things like how’s your mum, congratulations on your sister getting engaged, Berlin is a lovely place how was your holiday, your children are cute, what a lovely brunch etc. Their mum still cooks their breakfast, any annual leave is spent travelling with parents or, rarely, a girls’ trip. There’s nothing particularly wrong with any of it, but I don’t feel like we’re having meaningful conversations or that I particularly look forward to seeing them.</p>
<p>They’ll suggest arranging a Christmas get-together, basically saying they’re free any weekend in December and I’ll find myself looking at the dates and getting a sinking feeling that I can’t say I’m busy literally every weekend and every evening (although I’ve previously done that for a summer catch up). Or I’ll actually go and spend a rare child-free evening sitting there thinking what a waste of a night this is. They’re happy to come to where I live but because it’s a 1hr journey they obviously can’t come for a 5 min coffee.</p>
<p>I also find that I have very little interest in hearing about their careers or their (non existent) dating lives. I know that sounds awful, but I just don’t feel invested in those things anymore. I think part of what makes this difficult is the history. We’ve grown up together, shared so many milestones and they’ve stood beside me at my wedding. It feels almost wrong to consider walking away from friendships that have been such a big part of my life. I think I’m holding onto them purely because of how long we’ve known each other, rather than because I actually enjoy the friendships now.</p>
<p>Am I being unnecessarily dismissive and should I make more effort to maintain these friendships? Or is it perfectly reasonable to accept that we’ve grown apart?</p>
<p>And, practically speaking, how do you drop a friendship like this without causing a huge drama? Do you just stop responding, politely decline invitations and let things naturally fizzle out? Or do you actually have a conversation? I don’t want a big falling-out or to hurt anyone. I just don’t really want to keep making time for friendships that I’m no longer enjoying.</p>

id="item-5600149__content"><!--[--><!----><div class="prose break-words leading-6 text-card-foreground line-clamp-2"><p>My brother and his wife split up in January, he said it came from the blue and was the wife’s fault who ended it. They had a baby six months and a three year old. She accused him of having an affair which we thought was ridiculous. Turns out he was having some sort of affair with a woman from work 15 years his junior. Then six months later he got the younger woman pregnant before the divorce was even through.</p>
<p>He is having the kids which he said he dotes on minimal time (every other week), the wife took most of the money in the split, it wasn’t much to start with due to £60k of debt that had to be paid. The ex is now offering more time with the kids so she can work more and he is refusing.</p>
<p>i have two kids too; one nine one toddler and I’m finding it so hard to explain this. We live quite far away so don’t see him much, but when we visit my mother he comes and we have to pretend it’s fine. He just one day turned up with this girl, he didn’t introduce her properly he just brought her in, and went from saying he wasn’t having an affair to he’s moving on 11 months after the split but the girl is already far along in the pregnancy.</p>
<p>I’m so fed up of having to go along with his nonsense, he needs constant ego stroking and if anyone questions him he cuts them off and can be extremely cruel and personal. He twists everything that nothing is his fault. I try not to judge, we’re all fallible but I’ve known him his whole life and seeing him destroying life and life is awful.</p>
<p>I am not in touch with the old sister in law, we were never close and when it all kicked off we supported him wholeheartedly because we believed him. I don’t particularly like her but I feel so bad for her and the kids. He’s now moved on and still sees his kids but minimal time, he says the new kid will be better as his new gf is smarter. It breaks my heart.</p>
<p>Selfishly I’m also annoyed and upset that whenever we visit my family home we have to deal with him coming and explain to my 9yo what her uncle has done (left wife / got a new baby coming), we will of course love and support the new baby and hope to have a relationship with him or her but I’m also on tenterhooks that he’s going to hurt this new girl, she’s young and has been lovebombed and is now stuck with him and he’ll likely do the same as with the first wife.</p>
<p>How would you manage this / explain it to your kids? There’s nothing I can do about it and it’s none of my business but I feel I know him better than anyone.</p>

    /**
     * Sync Sourcepoint consent status to backend
     * @param {string|undefined} consentUUID - Consent UUID from Sourcepoint (undefined for non-GDPR)
     * @param {object} info - Consent info object from Sourcepoint
     */
    function sendConsentToBackend(consentUUID, info) {
        const payload = {
            consentUUID: consentUUID ?? null,
            consentedToAll: info.consentedToAll ?? null,
            applies: info.applies ?? null,
            categories: info.categories ?? {}
        };

        console.log('Syncing consent payload:', payload);

        // Wait for DOM to be ready to ensure page request has completed
        const sendConsent = () => {
            fetch('/consent', {
                method: 'POST',
                headers: {
                    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
                    'Accept': 'application/json',
                    'X-CSRF-TOKEN': 'ncNFTJuxWz4GcgW4L7FPtGAMDuclEE2T3iUJDc4y',
                },
                body: JSON.stringify(payload)
            })
                .then(response => {
                    if (!response.ok) {
                        throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
                    }
                    return response.json();
                })
                .then(data => console.log('Consent synced:', data))
                .catch(err => console.error('Consent sync failed:', err));
        };

        // If DOM already loaded, send immediately. Otherwise wait.
        if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', sendConsent);
        } else {
            sendConsent();

            const rawPreference = localTheme || cookieTheme || "light";

            root.classList.remove("light", "dark", "system");
            root.classList.add(active);
